distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): evaluative-decision affective priming with word primes and targets (Fazio et al. 1986, R0074).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): cue-word autobiographical recall of emotional versus neutral episodes (cue-word method of R0073); no external affective stimulus.
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): word-pair dot-probe task (MacLeod, Mathews & Tata 1986, R0072).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): colour naming of emotional versus neutral words; origin publication still TBD (D-032).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): event-related presentation of single emotional versus neutral faces with an orthogonal or passive task (ERP lead R0846). Differs from EMO-FACE-002 (blocked face-versus-shape matching).
Criteria 1 and 3 versus EMO-FACE-001: blocked face-versus-shape matching contrast instead of event-related emotional-versus-neutral faces (Hariri et al. 2002).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): single-session differential conditioning with one CS+ and one CS-, acquisition followed by extinction (lead R0951; authors not in literature.csv). Differs from EMO-FC-002 (graded generalization stimuli) and EMO-FC-003 (extinction recall on a separate day).
Criterion 1 versus EMO-FC-001: the condition set adds graded generalization stimuli between CS+ and CS-, so the contrast is a similarity gradient rather than CS+ versus CS- (lead R1010).
note: former variant "Fear generalization (parametric CS similarity gradient)"

distinguishing: Criterion 3 versus EMO-FC-001: multi-session structure with acquisition and extinction on one day and an extinction-recall test on a later day (leads R0276, R0933).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): standardised film set targeting discrete emotions with self-report after each clip (lead R0918, Cognition and Emotion, doi 10.1080/02699939508408966; authors not in literature.csv). Differs from EMO-FILM-002 (music videos with dimensional ratings), -003 (three valence classes) and -004 (four emotion classes).

Criteria 1 and 2 versus EMO-FILM-001: targets are continuous self-rated dimensions (valence, arousal, dominance, liking) rather than discrete emotion categories, and the stimuli are music videos rather than film clips (DEAP, Koelstra et al. 2012).
note: D-018; former variant "Music and music-video emotion elicitation"; S2-01, F01

distinguishing: Criterion 1 versus EMO-FILM-001: three valence classes (positive, neutral, negative) instead of a set of discrete target emotions; used by the public SEED dataset (Zheng & Lu 2015).
Criterion 1 versus EMO-FILM-001 and EMO-FILM-003: four emotion classes (happy, sad, fear, neutral); used by the public SEED-IV dataset.
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): funny versus non-funny cartoon viewing with ratings (Mobbs et al. 2003, R1184).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): passive viewing of pleasant, neutral and unpleasant pictures (ERP lead R0865).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): monetary incentive delay task with gain, loss and neutral cues and per-trial outcome feedback (Knutson et al. 2000, R0193). Differs from EMO-MID-002 (social reward cues and feedback).
Criterion 2 versus EMO-MID-001: incentive cues and outcome feedback are social (facial approval) instead of monetary (Spreckelmeyer et al. 2009, R0426).
note: D-025; former variant "Social incentive delay (social reward cues)"

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): two-condition look-versus-reappraise design with negative pictures (Ochsner et al. 2002, R0232). Differs from EMO-REG-002 (reappraisal contrasted with expressive suppression).
Criterion 1 versus EMO-REG-001: the condition set adds expressive suppression as a second regulation strategy (lead R1065; multi-strategy designs in R0599).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): emotional versus neutral speech prosody with passive listening or emotion identification; origin publication TBD (first_source holds an early ERP study, D-031).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): Trier Social Stress Test with a live panel (Kirschbaum et al. 1993, R0108). Differs from EMO-STRESS-002 (in-scanner arithmetic with time limits and performance feedback).
Criteria 1, 2 and 4 versus EMO-STRESS-001: computerised in-scanner arithmetic with rest and control conditions instead of a live panel, and per-item performance feedback (Dedovic et al. 2005).
note: MIST; named in class name, no variant before

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): NPU-threat test contrasting predictable and unpredictable threat with a neutral condition (Schmitz & Grillon 2012 protocol paper, sprint-2 S2-04).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): slow brush stroking versus control touch (Olausson et al. 2002, R1183).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): rapid serial presentation of emotional and neutral words during reading (Kissler et al. 2007, R1181).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): Frith-Happé animations in three categories (Castelli et al. 2000, R1189).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): point-light biological motion versus scrambled control (display method of Johansson 1973, R0029).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): rate-feedback-rerate conformity design with per-trial group feedback (Klucharev et al. 2009, R1187).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): Cyberball inclusion followed by exclusion (Williams, Cheung & Choi 2000, sprint-2 F06).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): dictator game with a passive anonymous recipient (Forsythe et al. 1994, R0114). Differs from SOC-DICT-002 (donation decisions to real charities).

Criterion 1 versus SOC-DICT-001: the recipient is a real charity and trials contrast voluntary giving with self-reward or mandatory transfer, rather than a single allocation to a passive person (Moll et al. 2006, R0341; Harbaugh et al. 2007, R0371).
note: donation variants were part of the -001 description (union); R0371

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): live eye contact versus photograph with dual-brain fNIRS (Hirsch et al. 2017, R1191).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): non-predictive gaze cueing (lead R1059). Differs from SOC-GAZE-002 (gaze-contingent interactive joint attention).

Criteria 1 and 4 versus SOC-GAZE-001: initiating versus responding joint-attention conditions, and the partner's gaze is contingent on the participant's own gaze (closed loop) instead of a pre-programmed cue (leads R0986, R0966).
note: interactive versions were part of the -001 description (union); R0966

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): standard IAT block sequence (Greenwald et al. 1998, R0165).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): finger-movement imitation-inhibition task (Brass et al. 2000, R0188).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): dyadic rhythmic finger movements with and without vision of the partner (Kelso et al., phi complex, R1172).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): personal versus impersonal versus non-moral dilemmas (Greene et al. 2001, R1186).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): passive own-name oddball (Berlad & Pratt 1995, R1185). Differs from SOC-NAME-002 (instructed counting of own or other target name).

Criterion 1 versus SOC-NAME-001: instruction conditions (count own name, count other name, passive) are added, so the contrast is voluntary attention to a name rather than self-relevance alone (Schnakers et al. 2009).
note: counting instruction was part of the -001 description (union); S2-12

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): cue-based self/other pain paradigm with a present partner (lead R0920). Differs from SOC-PAIN-002 (pictures of body parts in painful situations).
Criterion 2 versus SOC-PAIN-001: pictures of body parts in painful situations instead of symbolic cues signalling pain to a present partner (leads S2-10, R0919).
note: pictures were part of the -001 description (union); R0919

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): race and gender face categorisation with ERPs (Ito & Urland 2003, R1190).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): revised Eyes test with a control judgement (Baron-Cohen et al. 2001, R0214).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): self versus familiar versus unfamiliar face recognition; origin publication TBD (D-031).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): social judgment paradigm with expectancy-crossed feedback (Somerville et al. 2006, R1188).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): unexpected-transfer false-belief story with control questions (Wimmer & Perner 1983, R0060). Differs from SOC-TOM-002 (fMRI localizer contrasting false-belief and false-photograph stories).
Criteria 1 and 3 versus SOC-TOM-001: the control condition is a matched false-photograph story rather than reality questions, presented as a blocked fMRI localizer (Saxe & Kanwisher 2003, R0260).
note: former variant "fMRI false-belief localizer (false belief vs false photograph)"

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): third-party punishment of a dictator (behavioural origin, R1174).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): one-shot investment game between anonymous partners (Berg, Dickhaut & McCabe 1995, R0127). Differs from SOC-TRUST-002 (iterated prisoner's dilemma) and SOC-TRUST-003 (multi-round trust game with a fixed partner).
Criteria 1 and 3 versus SOC-TRUST-001: symmetric simultaneous cooperate/defect choices over repeated rounds instead of a sequential one-shot investment (Rilling et al. 2002, R0217).
note: prisoner's dilemma was part of the -001 description (union)

distinguishing: Criterion 3 versus SOC-TRUST-001: repeated rounds with the same partner, so that trial outcomes depend on the interaction history (King-Casas et al. 2005, R0312). Dual-brain recording is not itself a numbering criterion (D-021).
note: D-021; former variant "Hyperscanning: multi-round trust game with both players scanned" (hyperscanning kept as variant of -003)

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): single-round responder decisions (Guth et al. 1982, R0054).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): self versus other visuospatial perspective judgements; origin publication TBD (first_source holds an fMRI study, D-031).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): weapons identification task (Payne 2001, R0212).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): anaesthetic induction and emergence with responsiveness probes; origin of the experimental protocol TBD (first_source is the bispectral analysis method, R0111).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): closed-loop in-phase auditory stimulation versus sham (Ngo et al. 2013, R1192). feedback=discrete records the closed loop: each sound is triggered by the ongoing EEG; the sleeping participant receives no feedback display.
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): serial awakening paradigm (Siclari et al. 2017, R1193).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): event-related lane-departure task where response time to each deviation labels drowsiness (Lin et al. 2005, R1176). Differs from STA-DRV-002 (continuous driving with an eye-tracking vigilance label).
Criteria 2 and 3 versus STA-DRV-001: no lane-departure events, and vigilance is labelled continuously from eye tracking rather than from response times to discrete events (SEED-VIG dataset).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): inter-subject correlation of EEG during repeated or scrambled film viewing (Dmochowski et al. 2012, R1178).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): induction versus rest and control conditions in high and low hypnotizables; origin publication TBD (first_source holds an fMRI study, D-031).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): MATB with workload set by subtask rate and number (R1064/R0849); the number of workload levels is a parameter.

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): meditation blocks versus baseline; meditation style (focused attention, open monitoring) is kept as a parameter for now (split_log).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): experimenter-initiated thought probes (probe-caught; Antrobus et al. 1970, R0020). Differs from STA-MW-002 (participant-initiated self-caught reports).
Criterion 3 versus STA-MW-001: reports are initiated by the participant whenever they notice mind wandering (self-paced), instead of being elicited by experimenter-timed probes.

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): operant training of one EEG frequency band with continuous feedback over sessions (earliest seen: Sterman & Friar 1972, SMR). Differs from STA-NF-002 (haemodynamic regional neurofeedback in regulate/rest blocks).
Criteria 1 and 3 versus STA-NF-001: a regional haemodynamic signal is trained in alternating regulate and rest blocks, instead of continuous training of an EEG frequency band (Weiskopf et al. 2003).
note: D-020; former variants "Real-time fMRI neurofeedback of regional BOLD" (moved) and "fNIRS haemodynamic neurofeedback" (kept as variant of -002)

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): within-subject drug versus placebo resting recording; origin publication TBD (first_source holds a neural study, D-031).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): 10-minute visual PVT with response-time display after each response (Dinges & Powell 1985, R0070).

Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): one continuous rest run without a task (Biswal et al. 1995, R0124). Differs from STA-REST-002 (alternating eyes-closed and eyes-open blocks).
Criteria 1 and 3 versus STA-REST-001: two eye conditions alternate in blocks within a run, so eyes-closed and eyes-open rest are contrasted (Barry et al. 2007, R0362).
note: alternating blocks were part of the -001 description (union)

distinguishing: Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): binary negativity/positivity training with continuous visual SCP feedback, no spelling; the configuration from which the speller (STA-SCP-002) was built.
Criterion 1 versus STA-SCP-001: the two SCP classes are mapped to selecting or rejecting letter groups in a binary spelling tree, so trials yield character selections (Birbaumer et al. 1999, R1177).
Standard configuration (earliest published or canonical; D-057 -001): 30-s epochs scored into six R&K stages (Rechtschaffen & Kales 1968, R1180). Differs from STA-SLP-002 (AASM five-stage scheme).
Criterion 1 versus STA-SLP-001: five AASM classes (stages 3 and 4 merged into N3; REM renamed R) instead of six R&K stages (Iber et al. 2007).
